observation.visible_scene: A horizontally held ice-cream bar on a flat wooden stick against a uniform dark gray/black background. The bar is cream-colored with brown speckles, has a glossy highlight on its rounded left tip, and a dark chocolate-and-crunch coating where the stick enters on the right. The stick points right. The object is held essentially still throughout; no camera pan/zoom is evident.
visible_changes: For the first ~10 frames the lower contour shows only small static wavy bulges.
Around frames 11-25 the second bulge from the left on the lower edge slowly swells and elongates downward into a hanging droplet (a growing protrusion, not a translation of the whole bar).
Frames 26-27: the droplet stretches into a thin vertical strand with a rounded head.
Frame 28: the strand becomes very thin (necking) and a faint droplet/line is seen separating below it.
Frame 29: only a short faint vertical line remains under the bar, i.e. the drip has pinched off and is leaving the frame.
Frames 30-41: the elongated drip is gone; the lower edge reverts to a small rounded protrusion at that spot, with the leftmost bulge unchanged.
The body, stick, chocolate end and background positions stay constant across the segment (no overall motion).
outside_clip_unknowns: What is below the frame (whether the falling drip lands on anything).
Whether melting continues or other drips form before/after this excerpt.
The heat source or cause of the melting.
The exact start of the drip formation (it is already in progress by the time it becomes noticeable).
uncertain_details: The precise frame of detachment (between 28 and 29).
Whether the faint mark in frame 29 is the falling strand or a residual drip.
Tiny apparent shifts of the bar are within held-object jitter; camera motion cannot be confirmed from the static background.
